## 1. What already exists

`packages/backend/src/services/brand-theme/` — pure, dependency-free TypeScript.
No Prisma, no Express, no React. 43 tests in `__tests__/`.

| File | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `palettes.ts` | **Generated.** Tailwind v4 (286 entries) + IBM Carbon (10 families) + `CARBON_CATEGORICAL_ORDER`. Do not hand-edit. |
| `color.ts` | sRGB/OKLCH/OKLab/HSL conversions, `perceptualDistance`, `contrastRatio`, `parseHslTriplet`. |
| `color-story.ts` | Ranks a brand's colours into roles: primary, accent, ambient, dark/light anchors. Warns on stock-status hue bands. |
| `snap.ts` | Role-aware snapping onto the Tailwind palette. `CHROMA_WEIGHT`, `chooseFamily`, `isMuddy`, `mudEscapeFamily`. |
| `tokens.ts` | `BRAND_TOKENS` (25), `STOP_MAP`, `CONTRAST_PAIRS`, `CONTRAST_FLOOR`, protected families, `UNDERIVED_SHELL_TOKENS`. |
| `derive.ts` | `BrandInput` → `TokenMap`. The entry point: `deriveTheme()`. |
| `serialize.ts` | `serializeHslTriplets` (v1.7.0), `serializeOklch` (v1.7.5), `serializePrintHex` (PDF). |
| `charts.ts` | `brandAlignedCarbonOrder`, `seriesColor`. |
| `validate.ts` | `contrastFindings`, `chartContrastFindings`, `auditAllCombinations`. |
| `review-list.ts` | Eighteen tokens the user flagged for later review. |

Regenerate the palette with:

```bash
cd packages/backend && npx ts-node --transpile-only scripts/generate-brand-palettes.ts
```

`__tests__/palette-drift.test.ts` fails if the committed file and its sources
disagree, so a Tailwind upgrade surfaces immediately rather than silently.

### The core design, in one paragraph

A theme is **two family choices plus a fixed role-to-stop map** — not arithmetic
on lightness and chroma. Brand colours snap to the nearest Tailwind v4 entry;
accents snap within the 17 chromatic families and surfaces within the 9 neutral
ones; the stop for each token comes from `STOP_MAP` and is a property of the
token's *role*, not of the palette. This makes the configurable space finite at
**17 × 9 = 153 themes**, so `contrast-proof.test.ts` walks all of it and proves
every theme an operator can reach. Keep that property. If you add a token, add
its stop rule and its contrast pair, and the proof will tell you if you broke
something.

## 2. Phase 1 — persistence and delivery

**Goal:** activate a saved configuration and the whole app changes identity with
no rebuild and no flash.

### 2.1 Schema

Add to `packages/backend/prisma/schema.prisma`. Follow the existing
singleton-plus-JSON precedent — see `LottoQueueIntegrationConfig` (line ~459)
and `OperatingHoursRevision` (line ~33) in the same file.

Requirements:

- One active configuration per deployment. **Not multi-tenant.** No `tenantId`,
  no agency filter. `AGENTS.md` opens with why: the `ownerId` partition torn out
  in `ISSUES.md` #31 was this mistake at smaller scale.
- Store the brand *inputs* (the ranked hierarchy, family overrides, identity
  strings, capability flags) as JSON, not the materialized token set. A
  materialized theme silently disconnects from its inputs.
- Support draft vs active. A configuration can be saved without activating.
- Assets (logo light, logo dark, square mark) stored **in the database**, so
  they ride the existing backup/restore path. Cap upload size; the Pi's card is
  a known constraint (32GB, see the build-and-deploy memory note).

Migrations auto-apply on container start via the backend Docker `CMD`. Back up
`production.db` before anything destructive.

### 2.2 Resolution, fail-closed

Mirror `~/Repos/lotto/src/lib/brand-config/resolve.ts`. Order:

1. Active `BrandConfiguration` row
2. Compiled William Temple House default

Any storage error, invalid payload or derivation failure **falls back to the
compiled default** and surfaces the failure in Settings → Customization. A
broken saved appearance must never take down a public surface. This contract is
load-bearing; copy it verbatim in spirit.

### 2.3 Delivery — the part that differs most from LOTTO

LOTTO injects theme CSS into its server-rendered Next.js layout. FEED has no
render step: `packages/frontend/index.html` is a static build artifact served by
nginx with `try_files` (`docker/nginx.conf`).

Do this instead:

- A backend route (e.g. `GET /api/brand/theme.css`) returning
  `serializeHslTriplets(deriveTheme(config).tokens)` with `Content-Type:
  text/css` and a strong `ETag`.
- One **render-blocking** `<link rel="stylesheet" href="/api/brand/theme.css">`
  in `packages/frontend/index.html`, after the existing stylesheet references.
  nginx already proxies `/api/`. A stylesheet in `<head>` blocks paint by
  default, so there is no flash and no bootstrap script.
- Serve `304` on a matching `If-None-Match`. Bust the ETag on activation.

**Cascade note.** `index.css` declares its tokens inside `@layer base`. Layered
styles lose to unlayered ones, so an unlayered brand stylesheet wins without
`!important`. Verify this rather than assuming it.

**Three-state theme model.** `serialize.ts` already emits `:root, .light`,
`.dark`, and a `@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark) { :root:not(.light) }`
block. Do not collapse these — `docs/frontend-services/theme-control.md`
explains why all three states must work.

### 2.4 Frontend brand context

Identity strings (organization name, app name, tagline, links) need a React
context so components stop hardcoding "William Temple House". Do **not** convert
every string in this phase — establish the context and convert the auth screens,
`AboutPage` and the sidebar. The full list is in the plan's measured table.

### 2.5 Backup and restore

Include the brand configuration and its assets in the portable backup
(`docs/data-management/backup-and-restore.md`). A restored deployment should
come back fully branded.

### 2.6 Phase 1 gate

Seed a template row (William Temple House, and St. Johns Food Share as a second
template), activate it, and confirm the whole app changes with no rebuild and no
flash — sidebar, charts and all. Screenshot both themes.

## 3. Phase 2 — the Customization wizard

**Goal:** an administrator configures the appearance without a developer, using
a workflow identical to LOTTO's.

### 3.1 Build it on FEED's own stepper

`packages/frontend/src/components/ai-configuration/shared/BaseAIConfigDialog.tsx`.
LOTTO's Appearance wizard was itself built on the pattern inherited from this
component, so using it gives parity by construction. Look at
`packages/frontend/src/components/ai-configuration/steps/*` for step shape and
`setup/InitialSetupWizard.tsx` for a multi-step example.

Reference implementation to match step-for-step:
`~/Repos/lotto/src/components/appearance/appearance-wizard.tsx` and
`~/Repos/lotto/src/components/appearance/steps/*`.

### 3.2 Steps, in LOTTO's order

1. **Start** — from the WTH template, the St. Johns template, or from scratch.
2. **Identity** — organization name, app name, tagline, descriptions, links.
3. **Logos & icons** — upload light/dark logos and one square mark; measure
   dimensions server-side; generate derivatives. Preview the header slot at its
   capped height. (LOTTO's launch bug was a logo aspect ratio overlapping
   content on real phones — size by fixed *height*, never fixed width.)
4. **Colours** — extract the ranked hierarchy from the uploaded logo, show the
   snap **and its top three alternates**, let the operator reorder ranks. Live
   preview including a real chart, in light and dark.
5. **Staff copy** — sign-in heading, email guidance, placeholder.
6. **Capabilities** — any opt-in integrations.
7. **Review** — full preview, then Save draft or Save & activate.

### 3.3 Logo colour extraction

Port `~/Repos/lotto/src/components/appearance/palette-extract.ts`: median-cut
quantization over opaque pixels, ranked by **pixel population weighted by chroma
salience** so a small saturated mark beats a large pale wash. Feed the result
into `proposeColorStory()` which already exists in FEED.

This is the feature the user specifically asked for: the system should know
whether a logo is a two-tone brand or a multi-tone one — "is it Coke or Pepsi?"
— and let the operator correct the ranking by swapping ranks.

### 3.4 Where it lives

`packages/frontend/src/components/settings/index.tsx` becomes tabbed, on the
Analytics pattern (`packages/frontend/src/components/analytics/index.tsx`):

| Tab | Section | Scope | Who |
|---|---|---|---|
| General | Operating Hours | Organization | All staff |
| Appearance | Theme | This device | All staff |
| Appearance | **Customization** | Organization | Administrators |

**Gate the Customization section, not the Appearance tab.** `/settings` sits
outside the `AdminRoute` guard in `packages/frontend/src/App.tsx` and is
staff-visible. `AGENTS.md` is specific that the three-way light/dark/system
choice lives there; hiding the tab would take System away from every
non-administrator.

Do **not** auto-open the wizard on first sign-in — LOTTO decided against it
deliberately, because an interruptive modal can block an operator mid-incident.
Use a prominent call to action instead.

### 3.5 Phase 2 gate

Someone who has used LOTTO's wizard completes a from-scratch run with no
instructions.

## 4. Rules you must not break

- **One deployment per agency. Not multi-tenancy.** No `tenantId`.
- **Protected operational semiotics stay absent from the schema** — the four
  inventory status flags plus `destructive` and `success`. A saved configuration
  must not be able to express an override. `isProtectedToken()` guards the
  serializer; keep it.
- **Protected analytic semiotics** — `household`, `visit`, `person served` are
  never renameable. See `PROTECTED_TERMS` in `tokens.ts`.
- **The 153-theme contrast proof must keep passing.** If you add a token, add
  its stop rule and contrast pair.
- **Charts rotate `CARBON_CATEGORICAL_ORDER`, never re-sort it.** That order is
  deliberately hue-hopping for colour-vision deficiency.
- **Print always renders the light scope.** A report represents paper and must
  not follow the app theme (`AGENTS.md`, UI Standards).
- Use Shadcn/Radix components from `packages/frontend/src/components/ui`.
  `ScrollArea` needs a **definite** height, never only `max-h-*`.
- Page roots are exactly `space-y-6 min-w-0 w-full pt-6` with `SectionHeader`
  first.

## 5. Validation

```bash
# Backend — a plain single-project config, so this is genuine
cd packages/backend && npx tsc --noEmit          # expect 0 errors
cd packages/backend && npx vitest run            # expect 986 passed, 2 skipped

# Frontend — MUST name tsconfig.app.json; a bare `tsc --noEmit` checks nothing
cd packages/frontend && npm run typecheck        # expect exactly 227 (ratchet baseline)
cd packages/frontend && npx vitest run           # expect 445 passed
```

Never run `npx vitest` from the repo root — it picks up a config that fails 46
unrelated tests.

**Browser validation is required for UX work.** The user's dev server runs on
**port 5173** and is the only valid target; never start a second Vite process.
The app is behind magic-link OTP with no dev bypass — if you reach a login
screen, ask the user to authenticate rather than working around it. Backend must
be running on 3001.

Occasional flakes exist in the backend suite (supertest / "database is locked"
timing). Re-run before concluding a failure is yours.

## 6. Manual checklist before calling Phase 1 done

- [ ] Activate a seeded template; the app rebrands with no rebuild.
- [ ] Hard reload with cache disabled; confirm **no flash** of the default brand.
- [ ] Light, dark, and system (no stamp on the root element) all correct.
- [ ] Sidebar rebrands, not just page content.
- [ ] Charts pick up the brand-aligned Carbon order.
- [ ] Corrupt the stored payload deliberately; confirm the app falls back to the
      compiled default and reports the failure in Settings rather than breaking.
- [ ] A generated report PDF still renders light-on-white.
- [ ] Backup, wipe, restore; the brand comes back including assets.
- [ ] `docker/nginx.conf` proxies the new route in a production build.

## 7. Known issues to fold in or leave alone

- **`packages/frontend/src/test/chart-colors.test.ts` goes stale in Phase 1.** It
  reads `--card` from `index.css` and asserts 4.5:1. Once surfaces are
  configurable it keeps passing against the compiled default while a real
  agency's surface could fail. `contrast-proof.test.ts` supersedes it — delete or
  rewrite it as part of Phase 1.
- **FEED's dark focus ring is 1.50:1**, below the WCAG floor. Out of scope, has
  its own task. Do not silently absorb it.
- **`UNDERIVED_SHELL_TOKENS`** in `tokens.ts`: eight hardcoded `--feed-shell-*`
  gradient stops that do not follow a brand. They are gradients, not flat
  colours, so they need their own serializer. Phase 1 work if you have room;
  otherwise leave the constant as the record.
- **Eighteen flagged tokens** in `review-list.ts` — re-judge them in the browser
  once the wizard exists. Its test enforces that a resolved flag is removed.
